A reviewer claims this performance issue:
  title: Sequential awaits inside loop cause N+1 database queries
  lines: 3-3 (new file)
  rationale: Each iteration of the for-of loop awaits db.findUser independently, serialising all N queries. Total latency is the sum of all round-trips rather than the maximum. With large order sets this is a severe bottleneck.

The ONLY context you may use is this hunk:
File: orders.ts
Hunk: @@ -1,1 +1,3 @@
Lines show NEW-file line numbers; + added, - removed, space unchanged.
   1   async function enrich(orders) {
   2 +   const out = [];
   3 +   for (const o of orders) out.push(await db.findUser(o.userId));

Is the finding real and supported by THIS hunk? Try to refute it before agreeing. Report your outcome (upheld/refuted), your confidence, and your reasoning.

response.raw: {"outcome":"upheld","confidence":0.92,"reasoning":"The hunk shows `for (const o of orders) out.push(await db.findUser(o.userId))`, which awaits each db.findUser call sequentially per iteration. Because each await blocks the next iteration, N orders produce N serialized round-trips, making total latency the sum of all queries rather than running them concurrently (e.g. via Promise.all). This is the classic N+1 sequential-await pattern and is fully visible in the hunk itself; no external context is needed to confirm it. The only minor uncertainty is whether db.findUser truly hits a database or is cheaply cached/in-memory, but the method name and the await strongly indicate a real query, and the loop structure undeniably serialises whatever cost it has."}
